intent: Select a concrete bridge heatsink/fan assembly and connect it to Rust Gmsh/Elmer thermal evidence with source-bound replay, convergence, and safety checks. Keep numerical results conditional, preserve the open bridge current findings, and prevent stale or edited evidence from becoming an acceptance claim.

learnings.title: Solver-independence is not model-independence
learnings.note: The cooling evidence keeps numerical replay separate from assembled-cooker qualification.

learnings.title: External-FEM corroboration is a validity proxy
learnings.note: The change preserves an explicit unverified boundary for installed airflow, contact paths, and fault protection.

learnings.title: Qualification exports require clean-build replay
learnings.note: The retained bundle and replay checks bind generated inputs, process receipts, hashes, and semantic mutations.

residual_risks: The selected assembly remains a design requirement rather than a hardware qualification; installed airflow, contact resistance, package-to-lead coupling, ratings, and fault protection are still unverified.

The harness keeps a private net-to-trace/segment identity map in bridge_thermal.rs while neck_geometry.rs owns the corresponding bridge definitions; a future repair can update one map without the other and make current binding drift.
CoolingAssessment.status remains design_requirements_unverified even when numerical or PCB checks fail; downstream consumers must use compliance booleans and CheckReport findings for pass/fail.
The flexible run_with_scenarios API validates declared convergence links but does not establish that every future physical scenario has a complete three-resolution chain.
testing_gaps: Confirmed #1 (P2): no end-to-end PowerEntry runner test exercises contract propagation through runner::run; add integration coverage for valid, missing, and malformed contracts. The validator confirmed this gap. The committed power-entry.json is a production live-run artifact, but it is not a regression assertion for contract propagation.

current_tree_suppressions: Cooling reservoirs colder than ambient: validation now rejects both lower-bound branches and includes regression coverage.
Assembly relabeling bypass: validation pins the reviewed heatsink, fan identity, and quantity; mutation coverage exercises the assembly change.
Duplicate cooling current binding: run_with_contract now reuses bind_current_values shared with the retained thermal path.

Cooling safety/parser test gap: added tests cover assembly, qualification, load, failed-fan, and unknown-field rejection; remaining exact-boundary cases are not material to the current fixed contract.
Replay source-byte identity test gap: retained-only mutation now changes contract bytes while expected source bytes remain unchanged.
Convergence failure test gap: direct temperature, power, node-order, and missing-case mutations now fail validation.
Manifest evidence absence: the retained bridge-cooling evidence bundle is staged by the caller while the generated evidence directory remains excluded from files.txt.

validator.reason: The one-batch validator confirmed the runner contract-propagation coverage gap. It inspected the production power-entry.json live-run artifact, which demonstrates a run but is not a regression assertion.

coverage.cross_model: cross-model pass not run: prior host egress safety review rejected repository-code transfer; local adversarial reviewer used.
coverage.settlement: not evaluated: no plan was discovered (plan source none).
coverage.production_live_run_evidence: The committed power-entry.json is evidence that the production PowerEntry path ran with the cooling inputs; it does not exercise the contract-propagation regression assertion, so the confirmed P2 testing gap remains documented.
